name: Linear Search
description: Sequentially checks each element until the target is found or the array ends. Works on both sorted and unsorted arrays.
aim: Find a target by scanning left to right, comparing each element. Return the index when found or -1 if exhausted.
howItWorks: If no match: advance to next element

time.bestCase: Target is at the first position
time.averageCase: Expected n/2 comparisons for random target
time.worstCase: Target not in array — must check every element

complexity.spaceDescription: No extra memory — just a loop counter

realWorld: Finding an item in an unindexed file
Fallback when data is too small to justify sorting
whenToUse: Unsorted array where sorting overhead is not worth it
Single search on an array that won't be searched again
alternatives: Binary Search — O(log n) but requires sorted array
Hash Map — O(1) average for repeated lookups
Jump Search — O(√n) for sorted arrays
